text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَالُوا۟ لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمْ عَلَيْنَا ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍۢ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ

words.gloss_range: opening connective that resumes the prior testimony scene and carries it into quoted confrontation
words.prose: The opening {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps this speech event attached to the preceding exposure. The reader hears continuation before dialogue: the accused are reacting inside the same judicial scene, not launching a separate theological exchange.

topics.headline: opening continuation into confrontation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dialogue begins as a continuation of bodily testimony already underway.
topics.reason: The prefixed conjunction opens a new speech event while attachment evidence keeps it coordinated with the preceding witnessed exposure.

words.gloss_range: Form I plural saying that opens the humans quoted challenge without a separate lexical object
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, report, and verbal declaration; here the local frame selects reported dialogue inside a forensic scene
words.prose: With {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}), the humans enter the record through their own speech. The verb has no separate object because the quoted question supplies its content, and the plural ending makes the accused a collective voice whose speech-form will be mirrored by the skins. The contrast with bodily speech in 36:65 and the same-surah recurrence at 41:30, where the speech verb opens confession rather than accusation, sharpen this as a contested speech turn, not neutral conversation.

topics.headline: objectless speech verb opens quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the humans are exposed through direct quotation rather than summarized accusation.
topics.reason: The following quoted question supplies the speech content, so the verb functions as entry into a speech act.

topics.headline: collective human speech will be mirrored
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same plural speech-form first carries accusation and then prepares reversal by the skins.
topics.reason: The repeated speech verb at words 2 and 8 keeps the form constant while the speaker changes, and the later causative articulation distinguishes ordinary saying from made speech.

topics.headline: body-speech contrast and same-surah speech recurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 41:21 keeps human mouths speaking while other passages and later same-surah usage shift the speech setting.
topics.reason: 36:65 silences mouths while body parts speak, whereas 41:21 lets the accused question their skins; 41:30 uses the same speech verb in a confession setting.

words.gloss_range: addressing preposition governed by the speech verb, making the skins recipients of the question
words.prose: The small {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is doing discourse work: after the speech verb, it marks the skins as addressees rather than as the content of speech. Grammar grants the body surfaces interlocutor status before the answer explains how they can answer.

topics.headline: preposition makes skins addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owned body is directly addressed before it becomes the answering speaker.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the prepositional phrase as the addressee complement of the saying verb, not as a direct object or possession marker by itself.

words.gloss_range: their plural skins as possessed outer bodily surfaces, now singled out as adverse witness-interlocutors
words.root_gloss_range: skin, hide, outer covering, and related surface or lashing associations; here the local noun selects embodied outer surface as witness-bearing boundary
words.prose: In {{ar:جُلُودِهِمْ}} ({{tr:julūdihim}}), the witnesses are grammatically theirs, yet the possessed surface becomes a confronting other. The word names the outer boundary that touched the acts, so testimony comes from the body surface rather than from a detached observer; the wider skin, hide, and lashing field makes that same surface feel like both sensor and penalty-site. The movement from the witness list in 41:20 to the direct address here, and the concealment note in 41:22, makes skins the focal evidence-bearing surface; even the firm sound of the root reinforces the hardened boundary image.

topics.headline: possessed skins become confronting addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices self-alienation: what is grammatically theirs becomes a second-person witness against them.
topics.reason: The plural noun carries a possessive suffix, but the following address and answer recast that possessed body surface as a speaking participant.

topics.headline: outer covering becomes witness surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness is the embodied boundary that contacted the world, not an abstract body part.
topics.reason: The local noun selects the bodily skin sense, while the plural and witness pairing make the surface distributed and evidentiary.

topics.headline: listed witness becomes singled-out interlocutor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that skins move from one item in a witness list (41:20) to the singled-out addressee of the challenge, with 41:22 confirming the concealment issue.
topics.reason: The same-surah sequence moves from listed bodily witnesses in 41:20 to direct address in 41:21 and concealment from skins in 41:22.

topics.headline: consonantal hardness suits surface resistance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible firmness that matches the semantic picture of a hard outer surface resisting its owners.
topics.reason: The sound note is modest but locally coherent with the surface and resistance imagery already carried by the word.

words.gloss_range: contracted why-question asking the cause of already completed adverse testimony
words.prose: The interrogative {{ar:لِمَ}} ({{tr:lima}}) asks why the testimony happened; it does not undo the fact that it happened. Because the question is aimed at the skins, it mislocates agency as motive, and the answer redirects the demand for explanation to divine causation.

topics.headline: why-question scopes over completed testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question contests cause or purpose, not the reality of the testimony.
topics.reason: The contraction functions as a cause-question over the following completed testimony clause, with adversative force from the complement.

topics.headline: question treats skins as motive-bearing agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the humans ask the skins for motive, while the answer will move agency above the skins.
topics.reason: The reported record shifts into direct confrontation, and the coming causative answer repairs the wrongly aimed why-question.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural perfect testimony against the speakers, treating witness as accomplished and adversarial
words.root_gloss_range: presence, witnessing, and legal testimony; here the local complement selects adverse legal testimony while preserving presence as the basis of evidence
words.prose: The perfect verb {{ar:شَهِدتُّمْ}} ({{tr:shahidtum}}) addresses the skins as witnesses who have already testified. Its root-range joins presence and legal testimony: the skins can testify because they were present with the acts, and the following answer explains articulation without erasing that evidentiary presence. The bodily-testimony field in 24:24 and the move from narrated report to direct confrontation keep this witness act legally and dramatically present.

topics.headline: perfect second-person testimony is already complete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins are challenged after testimony has become an accomplished fact.
topics.reason: The perfect second-person form turns the prior narrated testimony into direct address without treating the testimony as pending.

topics.headline: presence becomes adverse legal evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why skin testimony is evidentiary: bodily presence at the acts becomes voiced legal witness.
topics.reason: The root range allows presence and testimony, while the local adverse complement selects legal witness; Form IV articulation later explains speech, not evidentiary access.

topics.headline: bodily testimony concentrates in skins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 24:24 distributes testimony across body parts, while 41:21 concentrates the answering witness role in skins.
topics.reason: The concrete parallel at 24:24 supports the body-as-legal-evidence field without controlling the local parse.

topics.headline: pronoun shift and sound intensify confrontation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the accused shift into first-person complaint while the addressed skins are pressed into the testimony verb.
topics.reason: The pronoun shift connects the prior third-person accused to the speakers, and the sound note reinforces the address point.

words.gloss_range: prepositional phrase marking testimony as adverse burden against the speaking group
words.prose: With {{ar:عَلَيْنَا}} ({{tr:ʿalaynā}}), the testimony is not neutral observation; it falls against the speakers. The attached first-person plural also exposes the split self: their skins are possessed as theirs, yet the complaint is voiced by an us standing under those skins as adverse witnesses.

topics.headline: preposition marks forensic burden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the testimony is directed against the speakers, not merely witnessed near them.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the prepositional phrase the complement of the testimony verb, and the preposition supplies adverse legal pressure.

topics.headline: first-person complaint divides owners from body
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a divided self: the owners speak as us while their own skins stand against them.
topics.reason: The shift from the possessive suffix on skins to the first-person plural object of adversity marks the same group from different sides of judgment.

words.gloss_range: second plural saying, now by the skins, introducing the explanatory answer
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, report, and verbal declaration; here the repeated Form I speech verb carries the skins answering turn
words.prose: The second {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) gives the skins a real dialogue turn. Their answer is not a confession of motive but an explanation of caused speech, so the repeated speech form mirrors the human accusation while reversing control. The convergence with body-speech patterns in 36:65 makes the skins both witnesses and answerers, and the immediate causative verb shows that their voice is real but derivative.

topics.headline: skins receive a plural speech turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins answer as speakers, but their answer reports cause rather than personal motive.
topics.reason: The verb introduces the quoted answer, and the following clause supplies explanation rather than confession.

topics.headline: skins combine speech and testimony roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 36:65 separates body speech and testimony roles, while 41:21 merges them in the skins.
topics.reason: The concrete parallel at 36:65 supports the broader body-speech field while the local speaker remains the skins.

topics.headline: same speech verb carries accusation and correction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a balanced exchange: the same speech form first carries accusation, then correction.
topics.reason: The repeated plural speech verb changes speakers while preserving the dialogue frame and audible cadence.

topics.headline: skin saying is interpreted by causative articulation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins truly speak in the scene, yet the next words define that speech as divinely caused.
topics.reason: The local echo from the speech verb to the causative articulation verb explains the source of the skins voice.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect causative: He made us articulate, with the skins as affected object before the named subject
words.root_gloss_range: articulate speech, intelligible expression, disclosure, and making speech manifest; here Form IV selects caused articulation by divine agency
words.prose: In {{ar:أَنطَقَنَا}} ({{tr:anṭaqanā}}), the skins say us before the named subject appears, so their new voice is foregrounded and then grounded. The Form IV causative makes articulation a bestowed capacity, not a property the skins independently owned. The root points to intelligible disclosure rather than mere sound, with 27:16 providing a contrast in taught nonhuman speech; the later repetition expands this local caused speech into a universal principle, and the hard consonantal release fits the move from silent skin to voiced answer.

topics.headline: object suffix foregrounds skins before agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the skins as affected recipients of speech before the named agent is heard.
topics.reason: The attached object suffix is part of the verb and precedes the delayed nominative subject, foregrounding the skins while preserving divine agency.

topics.headline: causative form assigns bestowed speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer dismantles the charge of betrayal by making speech a caused capacity.
topics.reason: The Form IV perfect marks completed causation and contrasts with autonomous simple speech.

topics.headline: articulation is meaningful, not noise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins produce intelligible testimony, not a mere bodily sound.
topics.reason: The root field supports articulate disclosure, and the why-question frame makes the disclosed answer responsive.

topics.headline: rare articulation root beside nonhuman speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 27:16 shows taught nonhuman speech, while 41:21 makes even skins articulate under divine causation.
topics.reason: The occurrence profile treats the root as constrained and mostly causative, and 27:16 supplies a concrete contrast for nonhuman articulation.

topics.headline: local articulation repeats and hardens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first caused speech opening into the later every-thing claim, with sound texture reinforcing the release into voice.
topics.reason: The same causative root recurs in the relative clause, and the sound note fits the pressure-release image of articulation.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as delayed nominative subject and governing agent of speech, creation, and return
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worshiped God, and contested derivational pressures of worship, bewilderment, or elevation; here the proper name fixes the recognized divine agent
words.prose: The proper name {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) identifies the cause of the skins speech as the named God, not abstract nature or bodily autonomy. From here the ayah builds one agency line: the named subject makes speech, is expanded by the relative clause, is resumed by the pronoun, and becomes the endpoint of return. The derivational dispute remains only as pressure around worship and awe, while 2:28 and the surah-local thread support the movement from life-giving agency to return. The full name also lands with weight before the relative clause expands His universal power.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins attribute their speech to the named divine agent, not to impersonal bodily power.
topics.reason: The proper noun is the delayed nominative subject of the causative verb and resists a generic deity or nature reading.

topics.headline: one agent spans speech, creation, return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a single authority line running from caused speech through creation to final return.
topics.reason: The named subject is resumed across the relative clause, explicit pronoun, and final pronominal endpoint.

topics.headline: derivational dispute adds awe without changing the proper name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship and overwhelming awe around the name, while the local grammar keeps the word as the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute can color the name but cannot replace the locally fixed proper-noun function.

topics.headline: life-giving and return field supports the authority chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 2:28 also moves from life-giving to return, while 41:21 inserts bodily testimony inside that authority pattern.
topics.reason: The concrete reference at 2:28 and same-surah recurrence both support, rather than create, the local chain of agency.

topics.headline: proper-name weight before expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the named agent landing with weight before the relative clause expands His power.
topics.reason: The sound observation coheres with the syntax: the proper name appears before the relative expansion.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun binding the universal articulation clause to the named divine subject
words.prose: The relative pronoun {{ar:ٱلَّذِىٓ}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) prevents the next claim from floating free. It first locks the clause to the named subject, then turns the local answer into an identifying action: the one who made us speak is the one who makes every thing speak. Its recitational stretch gives the hinge weight before the universal verb arrives.

topics.headline: relative pronoun binds clause to named subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the universal claim explains the named subject rather than introducing a new agent.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the relative as modifying the named subject and opening the following relative clause.

topics.headline: relative clause explains by enacted power
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that identity is given through action: the local maker of speech is defined by universal speech-enablement.
topics.reason: The postposed relative phrase expands the named subject and converts the answer into an attribute statement.

topics.headline: recitational delay before universalizing verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a held hinge before the claim expands from skins to everything.
topics.reason: The written long-vowel mark is a modest recitational cue that fits the structural delay before the universal verb.

words.gloss_range: repeated Form IV causative making every thing articulate as a settled divine capacity
words.root_gloss_range: articulate speech, explicit expression, and disclosure; here Form IV with a total object selects making entities intelligibly speak or disclose
words.prose: The second {{ar:أَنطَقَ}} ({{tr:anṭaqa}}) repeats the causative form and now takes a universal object. That repetition turns the skins own answer into a general principle: articulation is intelligible disclosure that can be caused across entities, not ordinary human vocalization. The earth reporting its news in 99:4 becomes a concrete parallel for nonhuman evidentiary speech, while the repeated root and sound thread bind the local and universal claims.

topics.headline: causative verb governs total object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second caused-speech verb is grammatically expanded beyond skins to total entityhood.
topics.reason: The verb is transitive and governs the following totality phrase, so the local event is generalized by grammar.

topics.headline: articulation becomes intelligible disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that caused speech here means intelligible disclosure from any thing made to speak, not merely human-style vocalization.
topics.reason: The root field supports articulation and explicit utterance, while the total object widens the channel to entities generally.

topics.headline: repeated Form IV escalates local to universal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a structural ladder: He made us speak, then He made every thing speak.
topics.reason: The same Form IV root is repeated, and the second instance interprets the first by expanding its scope.

topics.headline: 99:4 supports nonhuman evidentiary speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 99:4 gives a concrete parallel for nonhuman reporting, while 41:21 states the broader mechanism.
topics.reason: The occurrence profile makes the root salient, and 99:4 shows earth reporting as a parallel nonhuman witness scene.

topics.headline: tail generalizes the skin event audibly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the answer turning into a universal tail, with repeated consonants binding the movement.
topics.reason: The relative clause follows the local answer and the repeated root supplies an audible thread before the totality word.

words.gloss_range: accusative totality in construct, making exhaustive scope the object of caused articulation
words.root_gloss_range: allness, totality, entirety, and comprehensive inclusion; here the construct selects exhaustive scope over entities
words.prose: The totalizing word {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}) is not loose emphasis; it sits inside the object phrase governed by the causative verb. In construct with the following indefinite, it makes the scope exhaustive and open-ended. The every-thing formula also parallels divine command-power in 36:82 and fits the surah habit of expanding local scenes into comprehensive divine scope, while the compressed doubled sound gives the totalizing pivot audible weight.

topics.headline: totality is grammatically governed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that totality is structurally built into the object phrase, not added as decorative emphasis.
topics.reason: The word is accusative and in construct with the following noun, making exhaustive scope part of the governed object.

topics.headline: totality expands speech beyond skins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer refuses to treat skin speech as an isolated anomaly; any entity can fall under divine speech-enablement.
topics.reason: The heavily attested totality pair completes the escalation from local skins to universal object scope.

topics.headline: 36:82 links every-thing scope to divine power
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 36:82 puts every thing under creative command, while 41:21 puts every thing under possible articulation.
topics.reason: The concrete reference at 36:82 supports the local bridge between totality, command-power, and speech-power.

topics.headline: geminated sound gives totality weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compact audible weight at the pivot from skins to all entities.
topics.reason: The sound row gives a small but coherent payoff for the totalizing word.

words.gloss_range: indefinite singular entity under totality, opening the class of possible speakers to every thing whatsoever
words.root_gloss_range: thing, entity, object, affair, or existent datum; here the construct phrase selects broad created entityhood as object of caused articulation
words.prose: The indefinite {{ar:شَىْءٍۢ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}) completes the totality phrase by opening the class of possible speakers. It does not name animate beings only; it recasts the addressed skins as one instance of created entityhood. The hidden glorification of every thing in 17:44 and the surah-wide all-things field support this broader ontology, while the nasal ending audibly seals the universal phrase before the creation clause begins.

topics.headline: indefinite thing maximizes the object class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object class is every entity whatsoever, not a limited group of animate speakers.
topics.reason: The singular indefinite after totality functions distributively and broadens caused articulation to created reality.

topics.headline: thingness joins divine power and hidden expression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:44 makes every thing expressive beyond human grasp, while 41:21 makes such expression judicially intelligible when God makes it speak.
topics.reason: The concrete reference at 17:44 and same-surah recurrence support the all-things witness field.

topics.headline: skins become one case of larger ontology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the skins are no longer an odd exception; they are one instance within created entityhood.
topics.reason: The clause moves from addressed skins to every thing, structurally absorbing the local body surface into a universal class.

topics.headline: ending seals universal phrase before pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible boundary where universal entityhood closes before the answer turns to first creation.
topics.reason: The sound and cadence rows cohere with the syntactic boundary before the next coordinated clause.

words.gloss_range: connective before the explicit pronoun, linking universal speech to the creation claim without a hard break
words.prose: The connective {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) lets the answer pivot without breaking. It does not spell out because, yet it lets the creation clause ground the speech claim: the one who can make every thing articulate is also the one who first created the questioners.

topics.headline: wa before pronoun carries continuation and grounding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the creation statement is linked as explanatory continuation, not a disconnected doctrinal aside.
topics.reason: The conjunction before the independent pronoun can coordinate, resume, or mark circumstance, allowing explanation without an explicit causal particle.

topics.headline: connector pivots from made speech to made body
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the answer moving from present voice to original embodiment in one connected argument.
topics.reason: The connective joins the universal speech claim to the first-creation reminder, expanding accountability from testimony to origin.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person pronoun foregrounding the same divine agent before the creation verb
words.prose: The explicit pronoun {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) is not needed merely to mark the verb. It pauses on who before stating the act of creation, keeping the same divine agent continuous from caused speech through first creation and onward to the final endpoint.

topics.headline: pronoun foregrounds agent before verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the creation clause keeps the same agent in focus rather than drifting into a new topic.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun is explicit before a third-person verb and sustains continuity with the previously named subject.

topics.headline: pronoun joins speech, creation, and return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one third-person divine referent while the human addressee shifts across pronouns.
topics.reason: The pronoun chain maintains a single divine referent from the named subject to the final endpoint.

words.gloss_range: direct perfect creation of you, confronting the accused with their first embodied formation
words.root_gloss_range: creating, forming, originating, proportioning, and bringing into measured existence; here Form I selects direct origination of the addressed humans
words.prose: With {{ar:خَلَقَكُمْ}} ({{tr:khalaqakum}}), the answer turns from the skins us to the humans you. The root carries formed origination, and with the first-time phrase it points to initial embodied formation rather than generic making. Form I presents creation as direct divine action, unlike the causative speech verbs, and the clause becomes the hinge between universal articulation and final return. The parallels at 82:7 and 41:15 keep embodied formation and same-surah origin claims in view, and the back-of-mouth, stop-heavy texture suits the shift to foundational origin.

topics.headline: creation claim addresses the accused directly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the answer turning from the skins own us to the accused humans as created you.
topics.reason: The attached second-person plural object makes the questioners the direct object of the creation claim.

topics.headline: creation means first embodied formation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that bodily testimony is grounded in created embodiment, not in human ownership of the body.
topics.reason: The root field of creating and forming, together with the first-time phrase, selects initial embodied formation.

topics.headline: Form I creation needs no causative intermediary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast: speech is caused through another speaker, while creation is stated as direct divine origination.
topics.reason: The Form I perfect gives direct creative action, unlike the nearby Form IV speech verbs.

topics.headline: creation echoes embodied accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 82:7 linking creation and proportioning and 41:15 recalling the same surah origin claim, both clarifying embodied accountability here.
topics.reason: The concrete references at 82:7 and 41:15 support the local use of creation language as an answer to bodily testimony.

topics.headline: creation bridges speech and return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices creation as the hinge between caused testimony and compulsory return, with the sound texture matching foundational origin.
topics.reason: The clause sits between the every-thing articulation claim and the return clause, and the combined rows make origin the controlling frame for bodily witness.

words.gloss_range: temporal firstness in construct with the following instance noun, marking the origin point of creation
words.root_gloss_range: firstness, priority, beginning, and return-to-outcome associations; here the local construct selects temporal first occurrence rather than rank
words.prose: The word {{ar:أَوَّلَ}} ({{tr:awwala}}) is temporal, not a claim of superiority. In construct with the next noun, it makes creation a first occurrence in a sequence, so origin stands before destination. The broader first-creation argument is recognizable from 36:79, and here it is embedded inside the skins reply as the beginning of an accountability-return arc.

topics.headline: firstness becomes a first-time phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that firstness is measured as an occurrence in time, not as isolated rank language.
topics.reason: The word works with the following instance noun as a temporal construct qualifying creation.

topics.headline: origin point prepares final return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices creation as the starting point of a route whose other end is return to divine authority.
topics.reason: The local phrase selects temporal origin, while the final return clause makes that firstness the opening endpoint of an arc.

topics.headline: first creation answers restoration logic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 36:79 uses first creation to answer restoration doubt, while 41:21 uses the same logic inside bodily testimony.
topics.reason: The concrete reference at 36:79 and the local co-occurrence with creation and instance language support the first-creation argument pattern.

words.gloss_range: singular instance noun completing first-time construction and closing the origin phrase before return
words.root_gloss_range: passing, occurrence, instance, and a counted time; here the local noun selects a single counted occurrence of creation
words.prose: The noun {{ar:مَرَّةٍۢ}} ({{tr:marratin}}) completes the first-time construction. It turns origin into a counted instance, one pass through created existence that can be contrasted with later return. The restoration logic in 17:51 stands behind the move, while the matching nasal endings with the earlier universal entity phrase link all things to first occurrence before the next connective marks the boundary where the final destination clause opens.

topics.headline: instance noun completes firstness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the previous firstness becomes first time only because this instance noun completes it.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the previous word and completes the temporal construct.

topics.headline: creation becomes one counted occurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices first creation as a single traversed occurrence, not an indefinite origin.
topics.reason: The root and form support passage or occurrence, and the singular noun counts creation as one initial instance.

topics.headline: 17:51 supports return after first origin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:51 answers restoration by pointing to first origination, and 41:21 applies that logic to the accused.
topics.reason: The concrete parallel at 17:51 supports the origin-to-return reasoning without replacing the local phrase.

topics.headline: first occurrence closes before return opens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structure pivoting from the compressed origin phrase to the final return clause.
topics.reason: The word closes the first-creation phrase immediately before the next connective opens the return statement.

topics.headline: tanwin cadence marks the transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible transition from universal entityhood and first occurrence into return.
topics.reason: The cadence rows tie the phrase ending to the boundary before the final clause.

words.gloss_range: final connective coordinating the return clause with the creation clause as paired endpoint
words.prose: The final {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins return to creation rather than letting it sound like an afterthought. After the first-time phrase closes, the connective pivots the argument toward destination, making origin and return one coordinated claim about the same authority.

topics.headline: final connective joins origin and endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that return is paired with creation as part of one argument, not appended loosely.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the final return clause with the creation clause under the same authority line.

topics.headline: connector turns first occurrence toward destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the transition from first occurrence to final destination, including the audible release into the connective.
topics.reason: The connective follows the first-time phrase and opens the return clause, while the sound row reinforces the boundary.

words.gloss_range: fronted to-Him prepositional endpoint, fixing the destination of return before the verb is heard
words.prose: The phrase {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) places destination before the return verb. The endpoint is the same divine referent already named and resumed, so return becomes juridical recourse to authority rather than bare motion. Even where voice variation affects how the return is undergone, this fronted endpoint keeps the destination fixed.

topics.headline: destination precedes return event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the endpoint before the movement, so destination governs how return is heard.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is fronted before the return verb and functions as its complement.

topics.headline: pronoun resumes the named divine agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source of speech and creation is also the endpoint of legal return.
topics.reason: The suffix resumes the same divine referent across the ayah, turning return into recourse to named authority.

topics.headline: fronting holds endpoint despite voice variation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant agency in the return verb does not alter the destination.
topics.reason: The variant note is useful as apparatus: active or passive return changes agency, while the fronted endpoint remains stable.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural return verb, locally passive/imperfect in the base data, closing with compelled return to the fronted endpoint
words.root_gloss_range: returning, going back, restoration, recourse, and being brought back; here the local clause selects return to divine authority after first creation
words.prose: The closing verb {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}) makes return the ayah final landing point. In the base form, passive imperfect force makes the accused undergo a pending return while the fronted endpoint names where. The root completes the first-occurrence trajectory as restoration to authority, and accepted voice variation can shift agency without changing that endpoint. The creation-return pattern in 30:11 and the final plural cadence keep the addressed group present at the point of return, with the whole answer bracketed by divine agency.

topics.headline: passive imperfect foregrounds undergone return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices return as something impending and undergone, with destination clearer than the mechanics.
topics.reason: The base morphology is passive imperfect second plural, and the fronted endpoint is explicit while the returning agent is not.

topics.headline: root completes origin-to-return trajectory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices first creation and final return as one trajectory back to the authority that originated them.
topics.reason: The root range of return, restoration, and recourse is locally governed by the fronted endpoint and the first-creation phrase.

topics.headline: accepted voice variation changes agency, not destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that passive and active readings differ in how return is undergone, while the fronted to-Him endpoint holds the judgment constant.
topics.reason: The variant evidence is useful for agency contrast, but local fronting prevents it from changing the destination or closure.

topics.headline: 30:11 creation-return arc is compressed here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 30:11 pairs beginning creation with return to Him, and 41:21 compresses that arc into the skins reply.
topics.reason: The concrete reference at 30:11 supports the local creation-return closure and return-to-God formula.

topics.headline: final verb closes on collective return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer does not stop at testimony or origin; it closes with the addressed plural routed back to divine jurisdiction.
topics.reason: The final position, plural ending, fronted endpoint, and agency chain converge to close the ayah with return.

baseline_models.mechanism: Possessors address their own bodily envelopes as separate respondents; adverse testimony, a causative grant of speech, first creation, and return make the created body an evidentiary subject under its maker's jurisdiction.

activation_trace.role: The bodily envelope is grammatically detached as an addressed participant and supplies the material witness.
A knowledge-bearing declaration gives forensic force to the phrase 'against us.'
Intelligible articulation makes the skin a respondent, while the doubled causative assigns that faculty to God.
Original bringing-into-being grounds both divine authority over the body and the capability to activate it.
Return closes the movement by bringing embodied owners back under the same jurisdiction.

changed_reading.before: The skins miraculously talk during judgment.
changed_reading.after: The created bodily boundary is commissioned as an independent evidentiary subject and returns with its owner to the maker who can articulate it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: The universal scope of making every thing speak, together with branches for speaking indication and witness-sign, permits a second layer beneath vocal dialogue: created matter can be rendered legible as evidence.

activation_trace.role: The body's visible covering provides a surface on which embodied history can become legible.
A sign that bears witness widens testimony from a witness's report to an evidentiary mark.
Manifest indication supplies a nonvocal sense of speaking and makes universal articulation materially coherent.
A thing's meaningful indication lets the framing dialogue carry manifested meaning as well as uttered words.
Anything knowable and reportable supplies the unrestricted domain over which evidence can be made articulate.

changed_reading.before: God temporarily gives mute skin a human-like voice.
changed_reading.after: God makes every created surface semantically legible; the vocal exchange dramatizes a broader conversion of material traces into explicit evidence.

baseline_models.mechanism: Beginning, one temporal occurrence, and return form a loop around the speech event. The first maker does not add an alien faculty so much as reconfigure the measured creature during its passage back.

activation_trace.role: Activated articulation is the event whose place in the creation-return sequence must be explained.
Measured formation makes bodily capacity an originally ordered rather than autonomous possession.
Temporal precedence identifies creation as the first activation against which the speaking body is read.
A bounded temporal occurrence makes 'first time' imply a further passage rather than a static origin.
Being brought back completes the loop and locates renewed bodily disclosure within return.

changed_reading.before: First creation is a parenthetical proof that God can make skin speak.
changed_reading.after: The speaking body is a second configured passage of the same measured creature from first formation toward return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first supplies detailed, lucid recitation, then refusal to hear, and finally deliberate noise intended to defeat that recitation. The focus opens an alternative disclosure medium: the hearer's own matter is made to signify and testify, so suppression of the external message cannot suppress evidence.

activation_trace.role: Speaking indication anchors the changed reading in God's conversion of the body into a disclosure channel.
Knowledge-bearing testimony identifies the channel's output as evidence rather than mere sound.
Detailed clarification establishes an ordinarily explicit message whose reception is later contested.
Lucid articulation removes obscurity from the normal verbal disclosure channel.
Auditory perception is the reception faculty explicitly withheld from the clarified message.
Recited discourse is the precise target of the attempted suppression.
Mixed acoustic noise supplies the interference mechanism used against hearing.
Overpowering force names the intended result of controlling the soundscape.

structural_cues: 41:3-4 pairs articulated revelation with refusal to hear; 41:26 turns refusal into the tactic 'do not listen, make noise, prevail.'
The focus repeats causative anṭaqa and extends it to every thing, shifting disclosure from an external recitation to created matter.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an accessible recitation, refused hearing, and deliberate acoustic interference; I infer a directional shift to a bodily channel that cannot be jammed. A live alternative is that the recitation conflict and bodily testimony are parallel speech scenes without a causal channel replacement.

changed_reading.before: The skins speak only because a courtroom requires witnesses.
changed_reading.after: The skins are an unjammable disclosure medium: when hearers suppress articulated revelation, God makes their own created matter articulate the evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Early speakers place covers over inward reception, weight in ears, and a barrier between parties. Later concealment fails before hearing, sight, and skins because it rested on a false estimate of divine knowledge. Since skin is itself the body's covering, its speech reverses the claimed protective boundary into an exposing surface.

activation_trace.role: The literal bodily covering anchors the reversal from enclosure to disclosure.
Manifest indication turns the enclosing surface into an outwardly legible one.
Protective covering supplies the earlier model of an inward domain sealed from the message.
Weight in the ear materializes blocked reception at a bodily aperture.
Prevention of access extends enclosure from organs to the relation between speaker and hearer.
Covering and concealment identify the strategy that organ testimony defeats.
Uncertain supposition exposes the faulty epistemic premise behind attempted concealment.
Knowledge as disclosure to the knower supplies the divine reach that the covering cannot limit.

structural_cues: 41:5 locates blockage in hearts, ears, and the interval between parties; 41:22 returns to concealment and the hearing-sight-skin triad.
The possessive 'their skins' and adverse 'against us' make the owner's nearest boundary the point at which enclosure reverses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a sequence of covers, ear-weight, barrier, attempted concealment, and organ testimony; I infer that the body's covering is causally reversed into disclosure. A live alternative is a simpler contrast between worldly refusal and later judgment with no special boundary mechanism.

changed_reading.before: A body part unexpectedly betrays the person who owns it.
changed_reading.after: The very covering presumed to preserve a hidden interior is inverted into the surface through which that interior becomes public.

context_deltas.mechanism: Sky and earth are addressed and answer in willing compliance during creation; later dead earth moves and rises through renewed life, followed by power over every thing. These scenes make skin-speech one local activation of creation-wide responsiveness to its maker.

activation_trace.role: Bringing creatures into existence is the focus's explicit ground for their renewed responsiveness.
God-given articulation is the bodily instance generalized by the cosmic command-response.
Return makes the later revival scene relevant to the body's reactivated capacities.
Uttered address and reply give the sky-earth relation the same dialogic form as the skin exchange.
Compliance makes cosmic matter responsive rather than merely passive under command.
Earth's life-marking movement supplies a material transition from stillness to activated response.
Life returning to earth provides the surah's concrete reactivation analogy.
Loss of life sets the maximal incapacity that divine reactivation overcomes.
Effective capability over every thing makes the extension from revived earth to speaking skin explicit.

structural_cues: 41:11 places a two-party command and answer inside the first-creation sequence.
41:39 repeats 'every thing' after dead-earth revival, echoing the focus's 'made every thing speak.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a speaking, compliant cosmos and a visibly reactivated earth; I infer an ontology of creaturely responsiveness connecting those scenes to the skins. A live alternative is that 41:11 is rhetorical personification and 41:39 only an analogy for resurrection power.

changed_reading.before: Speaking skin is an isolated suspension of ordinary material incapacity.
changed_reading.after: Speaking skin is a concentrated instance of a surah-wide rule: creation can answer, move, and disclose when its maker activates it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate frame ties organ testimony to what people did; later recompense answers action, and the closing rule sends good to the self and evil against it while denying misplacement by the Lord. Bodily testimony is therefore the person's own action returning through the self's created substrate.

activation_trace.role: The owner's own bodily envelope keeps the evidence within the embodied self rather than importing an alien accuser.
Adverse knowledgeable testimony is the mechanism by which action becomes judicially reflexive.
Return supplies the directional movement by which embodied action comes back upon its agent.
Intentional deed is explicitly named as the content and cause of the organs' testimony.
Answering an act with its consequence supplies the judicial return relation.
Deliberate action is grammatically routed toward its own agent.
The thing's own self supplies the endpoint for both benefit and adverse consequence.
Harmful action supplies the negative content that returns against the self.
Putting something in a wrong place marks the injustice excluded when one's own action returns through one's own body.

structural_cues: 41:20 says the organs testify because of what their owners were doing; 41:21 then asks why the testimony is 'against us.'
41:46 balances 'for his self' with 'against it' and immediately denies injustice by the Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deed-based testimony, act-matched recompense, and action routed for or against the self; I infer that embodied evidence preserves and returns the agent's own deed. A live alternative is purely legal accountability with no claim that the body materially retains action.

changed_reading.before: The body betrays its owner by joining an external prosecution.
changed_reading.after: The owner's deed returns as evidence through the owner's own embodied self, making judgment reflexive rather than an alien accusation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The condemned supposition is that God does not know much of what they do, while the close declares God witness over every thing and completely encompassing every thing. Causing things to speak does not acquire missing information; it externalizes already encompassing knowledge into an undeniable public form.

activation_trace.role: Manifest indication is the operation that publicizes knowledge rather than producing it for God.
Knowledge-bearing declaration supplies the public evidentiary form.
Mistaken conjecture identifies the false model of limited divine access that the speaking body corrects.
Knowledge as the thing's disclosure to the knower names the capacity wrongly denied.
Witnessing over every thing generalizes the focus's local body-witness relation to divine knowledge.
Total inclusion gives the closing witness formula the same unrestricted scope as the focus.
Every knowable and reportable thing is already within the domain of divine witnessing.
Complete epistemic enclosure removes any informational gap that creaturely speech would need to fill.

structural_cues: 41:22 explicitly locates the failure in what they supposed God knew; 41:23 says that supposition destroyed them.
41:53-54 close with witness and encompassing formulas over every thing, repeating the focus's universal object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies false conjecture about divine knowledge followed by total witness and encompassment; I infer that creaturely testimony manifests knowledge for judgment rather than informs God. A live alternative is that testimony remains a formal judicial procedure whose epistemic purpose is left unstated.

changed_reading.before: God calls bodily witnesses to establish facts that require testimony.
changed_reading.after: God makes already encompassed facts publicly undeniable, correcting the deeper error that hidden deeds escaped divine knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing promise sets signs in distant horizons beside signs within selves until truth becomes manifest, then names God witness over every thing. The focus supplies a concrete inner sign: the body's visible boundary is made explicitly indicative and testifies.

activation_trace.role: The bodily covering gives the inner-sign system a concrete, visible surface within the person's own embodied self.
Speaking indication converts a latent bodily sign into explicit meaning.
Caused showing supplies the disclosure process by which signs become perceptible.
An evident sign names the category into which the speaking skin is newly placed.
Distant horizons provide the outer pole against which evidence within the self gains force.
The self as the thing itself locates the relevant signs inside rather than among foreign witnesses.
Emergence into clarity supplies the endpoint of the body's move from silent sign to testimony.
Truth fixed to reality is what the inward bodily sign discloses.
A witness-sign over every thing fuses the closing sign vocabulary with the focus's bodily witness.

structural_cues: 41:53 balances 'in the horizons' with 'in themselves' and gives both a single result: truth becomes clear.
Its final 'over every thing a witness' recombines the focus's roots for every thing and testimony.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies outer and inner signs that are progressively shown until truth is clear; I infer that the speaking skin is a concrete enactment of the inner-sign pole. A live alternative is that 41:53 promises general proofs and does not classify organ testimony as one of them.

changed_reading.before: The skin is a hostile informant standing over against the person.
changed_reading.after: The skin is also the nearest inward sign: evidence already within the self is made explicit until the truth cannot remain latent.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers botanic and gestational emergence into a testimony scene. It remains anchored in skin as bodily covering and in causative indication, while 41:47 sequences covered fruit, hidden carrying, delivery, knowledge, and witness. Render it only as a material analogy for emergence across a boundary, not as lexical equivalence or a reproductive interpretation of the focus.

activation_trace.role: The bodily covering supplies the boundary across which concealed evidence becomes manifest.
Causative indication supplies the transition from latent content to explicit evidence.
Knowledge already reaches both hidden process and outward event, framing emergence as disclosure rather than discovery.
Movement out of concealment supplies the directional transition assigned to testimony.
A plant's enclosing sheath supplies a material analogue for the skin-bound hidden interior.
Interior carrying supplies a model of content retained before outward manifestation.
Delivery supplies the terminal crossing from enclosed content into the public field.
The explicit absence of a knowledgeable witness at the scene keeps the material emergence tied to testimony.

changed_reading.before: The skin reports facts that were somehow stored in it.
changed_reading.after: Testimony can be imagined as an emergence event: what was carried behind a covering crosses its boundary into public evidence under knowledge that already enclosed it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation uses the packet's form-distant q-w-l to q-l-l split and is therefore deliberately strange. It remains anchored in the two focus occurrences of q-w-l and in the shift of speaking control from owners to skins, with 41:39 supplying an actual movement image. Render it only as a formal or affective resonance of destabilized discourse; do not translate qāla as 'tremble' or claim a direct lexical sense.

activation_trace.role: A fear-like tremor supplies an affective undertone to the owners' challenged control of the dialogue.
Instability and movement model the transfer of speaking authority from human questioners to bodily respondents.
God-enabled articulation is the force that destabilizes the owners' monopoly on speech.
Actual shaking and movement elsewhere in the surah gives the formal instability a contained material echo.

changed_reading.before: The two uses of 'they said' neutrally frame a question and answer.
changed_reading.after: At an exploratory formal level, the dialogue itself loses stability as human speech is displaced by God-enabled counter-speech from the body.

strongest_changes: The skin's ordinary covering function is reversed: blocked and concealed reception becomes involuntary bodily disclosure.
Cosmic command-response and dead-earth revival recast skin-speech as creation-wide responsiveness under the first Creator.
Action for or against the self and total divine knowledge recast testimony as reflexive public manifestation, not information supplied to God.
The closing signs within selves make the speaking skin an inward sign whose latent evidence becomes explicit.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context connected the focus not only to judgment but to a sustained conflict over disclosure media: detailed recitation, refused hearing, deliberate noise, bodily witness, inner signs, and total encompassment.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether anṭaqa should be rendered as audible speech alone or can also carry nonvocal material indication.
Whether cosmic address and revived earth imply a direct ontology of responsive matter or function only as analogies for divine power.
The sheath-emergence and q-w-l/q-l-l readings remain exploratory material and formal resonances.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Speech discloses a capacity already embedded in things.** **ن ط ق B001** gives articulated audible speech and **ن ط ق B002** speech-like indication; **ك ل ل B003** gives totality. The skin's answer expands from one organ to every thing. I infer that explicit speech is the unveiled endpoint of a broader created capacity to indicate. The event reads less as an alien faculty added to matter than as latent indication made articulate.
2. **Origin already points toward return.** **ء و ل B001** gives beginning, while **ء و ل B002** gives return to outcome or final meaning; **ر ج ع B001** gives return. “First time” and “you are returned” frame the same maker. I infer that origination establishes the competence and claim by which return occurs. The first making is therefore retrospective evidence for the final destination.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:39 supplies a visible material analogue: the one who revives earth can revive the dead. 41:47–48 later shows hidden processes and lost claims returning to decisive knowledge, reinforcing creation as an evidentiary path to outcome.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Material testimony can be articulated speech or speech-like disclosure.** Lexically, `ن ط ق B001` is articulated audible expression and `ن ط ق B002` speech-like indication by books, signs, or lessons; `ش ه د B002` supplies knowledge-bearing testimony. Structurally, skins answer a question, yet the clause broadens articulation to `كل شيء`, and 41:22 treats hearing, sight, and skin alike as unavoidable witnesses. I assign `أنطق` the role of making retained evidence legible. The abductive move is that disclosure may occur by articulate utterance or by an intelligible material indication; both accepted branches remain visible rather than being collapsed. The ayah reads as a general opening of normally mute evidence.

2. **First making grounds final return.** `خ ل ق B002` is originating into being, `ء و ل B001` beginning and precedence, and `ر ج ع B001` return or sending back. The first creation and return are placed in one sentence after the skins’ newly enabled speech. I assign origination the role of precedent for restoring capacities and return the role of bringing the created subject back to its source. The inferred arrow is that an agency able to initiate embodiment can reconfigure embodiment as witness. The return is thus read through continuity of creative control, not as an unrelated second event.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:22 showed that speech-like disclosure applies to hearing and sight as well as skin, broadening the material witness field. 41:26 then produced a sharp reversal: agents who tried to prevent meaningful speech from being heard encounter a world made able to speak.

baseline.text: Derilerine, Niçin aleyhimize tanıklık ettiniz? derler. Onlar, Her şeyi konuşturan Allah bizi konuşturdu. Sizi ilk kez O yarattı ve O'na döndürülüyorsunuz, derler.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The immediate sequel explains that the hearers, eyes, and skins testified because concealment could not evade divine knowledge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A record that speaks truthfully about deeds provides a distinct model of evidence at judgment alongside the speaking skins.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It connects the Creator with return to Him, supporting the focus's movement from first formation to final return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The book speaks truth against people by recording their deeds, a close parallel to the focus's embodied witnesses.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Hidden action is converted into ordered public evidence through forced assembly, embodied testimony, and disclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The body is not merely present at judgment; its apertures, hide, and tongue form an evidentiary apparatus.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Body Gives Evidence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Skin, ear, eye, and tongue become distinct witnesses that expose intentional work.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: skin as bodily sheath `quranic:root_000253:B001/m01`; hearing by the ear `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`; visual perception `quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`; presence with direct observation `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony that declares known fact `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; tongue as witness `quranic:root_000822:B005/m01`; articulated speech `quranic:root_001519:B001/m01`; an indication that speaks for itself `quranic:root_001519:B002/m01`; intentional work `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The body divides into evidentiary roles: ear and eye register, skin stores and appears, and tongue declares. The latent image of a sign that speaks for itself lets bodily material function as proof without depending on the defendant's chosen account.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealment Undone by Knowledge
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Attempted covering fails because conjecture about the observer is replaced by disclosed knowledge.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: covering and hiding `quranic:root_000674:B001/m01`; weak conjecture `quranic:root_000969:B003/m01`; suspicious disposition `quranic:root_000969:B005/m01`; inward unspoken thought `quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`; knowledge as disclosed recognition `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; insight of the heart `quranic:root_000121:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Covering presumes that sight can be managed from outside, but conjecture has already misdescribed the knower. Once knowledge is framed as disclosure, concealment and supposition collapse together.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2: Bad Estimate Becomes Material Ruin
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An unreliable estimate fixes the wrong location or outcome, then resolves as a fall and measurable loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Faulty belief becomes an unstable well-site, a stone cast into a drop, and capital removed from an account.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Unreliable Place of Expectation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person marks where a thing should be found, but the estimate has no dependable outcome.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: expected location or habitual place `quranic:root_000969:B002/m01`; conjecture without certainty `quranic:root_000969:B003/m01`; a well or affair whose outcome cannot be trusted `quranic:root_000969:B006/m01`; inward unspoken proposition `quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`; belief or doctrinal position `quranic:root_001272:B013/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Assumption is spatial before it is doctrinal: it marks a presumed site. The unreliable well-image makes the epistemic failure concrete, because the expected resource may not be present and the final depth cannot be trusted.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.

Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.

Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da gözle görülen düzensiz bir sarsılma veya titreme görünümü taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda nesne ve fiziksel kararsızlık kurucudur; komşu kolda insan bedeni ile korku veya öfke nedeni kurucudur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel sallama, hareketten doğan ses ve aynı kökteki duygusal titreme karşılaştırmaları fiziksel hareket çekirdeğinin sınırını en açık biçimde gösterir.

root_profile.summary: Kök, azlık; bir şeyin tepesi veya başı; büyük bir kap; yük taşıma, yükselme ve yola koyulma; korku ya da öfkeden titreme; nesnenin oynayıp yerinde duramaması ve hareket sesi olmak üzere altı ayrı anlam kolunda düzenlenir.
